qt: to the Commission Arkadiusz Mularczyk (ECR) Subject:

In its answer to Question E-004817/20251, the Commission recognised the return of the manuscript ‘Gaude mater Polonia’, looted from Poland by Nazi Germany during the Second World War, as a bilateral matter between Poland and Germany. The manuscript was returned to Poland on 17 June 2026 following provenance research and cooperation between institutions in both countries. The Commission also co-financed the Jewish Digital Cultural Recovery Project, which involved provenance research and the creation of a database of cultural property looted by the Nazis. This demonstrates the value of joint documentation, even when the return of a specific object takes place through bilateral cooperation. Many cultural objects removed from Poland, Greece and other occupied countries by Nazi Germany remain unidentified. 1.

Has the Commission assessed the gaps in cross-border access to archives, provenance data and information on the current holders of cultural property stolen by Nazi Germany during the Second World War? If not, will it carry out such an assessment?

Will the Commission propose a programme, accessible to all affected countries, for the digitisation of archives, common standards for provenance research and an interoperable database of missing objects, and what timetable does it envisage?
If it is not planning such a programme, what specific measures of a comparable scope will it take, and by when?
